Definition: from G5021; regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity:--order.
BiblicalUsage: The word is order, a fixed arrangement. Christ is a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec, and the writer asks what further need there was for another priest to rise after that order. Paul says all things must be done decently and in order, and he rejoices to see the order of the church at Colosse.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe order is God's way: the priesthood has its order, the church has its order, and nothing is left to confusion. My position is that the order of Melchisedec is better than the order of Aaron, because it does not end.
